messages:
noah: Heads-up: Sample-app fails in Vercel Edge after our dual-publish change. Repro: streaming + retry path. Node demo is fine. Anyone hit similar?

anya: Oof. Can you paste the runtime error and package.json exports?

noah: Error: 
```
TypeError: request.headers.get is not a function
    at buildAuthHeaders (dist/esm/auth.mjs:78:19)
    at retryIfNeeded (dist/esm/retry.mjs:34:12)
```
package.json excerpt: 
```
"name": "@redwood/sdk",
"version": "2.1.0",
"main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
"module": "dist/esm/index.mjs",
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  "./": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.mjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

frank: Sounds like our ESM output assumes Fetch API `Headers` while CJS code path used Node header objects. Edge runtime picked the ESM entry; bundlers (esbuild/webpack) also resolve to the import/default branch. Some code still treats headers as plain object.

sophie: Two options: 1) Add an explicit `edge` conditional export to point to an adapter-built ESM that wires fetch-based runtime adapters; or 2) refactor auth/retry to use a tiny HeaderAdapter interface and ship one ESM that selects adapter at runtime based on feature detection. I prefer #2 to avoid extra build artifacts.

noah: Runtime feature detection sounds nice but bundlers may tree-shake platform adapters unpredictably. If consumers bundle for edge, they might pull node-only adapters accidentally.

anya: Right. Pragmatic compromise: keep single authored ESM source with an adapter abstraction, but emit two named entrypoints during build: `dist/platform-node.mjs` and `dist/platform-edge.mjs`. Then use exports map with `node` and `edge` conditions so resolvers pick the right file. That keeps behavior deterministic and lets bundlers choose the intended platform. Example exports snippet: 
```
"exports": {
  "./": {
    "node": "./dist/platform-node.mjs",
    "edge": "./dist/platform-edge.mjs",
    "default": "./dist/esm/index.mjs"
  },
  "./types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

frank: +1. Also ship a tiny CJS shim at `dist/cjs/index.js` that does `module.exports = require('../dist/esm/index.mjs').default ?? require('../dist/esm/index.mjs')` so old require() consumers keep working without heavy CJS builds. Keeps CI lighter.

sophie: For typings: add explicit `"./types"` export and a small root `index.d.ts` that re-exports from `dist/types/index.d.ts`. Editors like VSCode will pick that up even if they follow conditional exports. Also add `typesVersions` for older TS compat.

noah: We also need to tighten our CI: add a matrix that runs Node 18 (native ESM), Node 16 (CJS shim), Cloudflare worker (wrangler), and Vercel Edge emulator. Smoke tests should include: streaming request + first request fails (502) then retry succeeds; verify headers shape and that auth middleware doesn't assume Node internals.

anya: One gotcha: esbuild bundling for consumers sometimes resolves conditional exports at bundle time and inlines the platform file. Document that in migration notes and recommend `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` (root import) instead of deep-importing platform files.

frank: Also add a tiny runtime assertion in dev builds that checks `typeof fetch === 'function'` vs presence of `process.versions.node` so the adapter is explicit and errors are clearer. Example: 
```
if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') {
  if (isNode && platformAdapterName !== 'node') {
    throw new Error('SDK platform adapter mismatch: build targeted edge but running in node');
  }
}
```

sophie: I'll draft the changelog entry and migration guide wording. Include recommended tsconfig for consumers: `{"moduleResolution": "bundler"}` for Vite/esbuild, or `"node16"` for node16-style resolution.

packager-bot: Draft PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/301 - adds platform adapters, edge/node exports, root index.d.ts, CJS shim, CI matrix for edge smoke tests. CI will run on push.

noah: Great. I'll add a small sample-app test that reproduces the original failure and attach it to the PR. Once CI passes we'll cut a patch release and notify customers.

frank: Thanks. If we can standardize on adapter interfaces and a clear exports pattern we can avoid these subtle runtime mismatches going forward.

anya: Agreed. Also add a note to dev SDK docs about bundler behaviors and deep imports.

noah: Thanks all  I'll follow up with the PR link and sample-app CI results. :ship:
